Empirical Research Plan – “Do the ‘Best Companies to Work For’ Create Shareholder Value?”

======================================================================
1. Identification Strategy
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Chosen design:  Staggered Difference-in-Differences (DiD) with an event-study
lead/lag decomposition, complemented by a short-run announcement event study.

Why it fits:

•  Treatment is discrete and occurs at an observed moment – first inclusion in the
   Fortune “100 Best Companies” list.

•  Firms enter (and sometimes exit) the list at different calendar years, giving
   natural staggered adoption that DiD can exploit.

•  A panel of monthly stock returns, plus firm fundamentals, exists for many pre-
   and post-treatment periods, allowing us to test and visualise pre-trends.

•  DiD with firm FE controls for time-invariant selection of intrinsically
   “better” firms; year (or month) FE purge economy-wide shocks.

•  A narrow-window  (–5, +5 trading days) event study around the publication date
   separately identifies whether information is immediately priced.

======================================================================
2. Treatment and Control
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
   Treated_it = 1 if firm i is in its FIRST year of appearing on the list and all
   subsequent months; 0 otherwise.

Control group  
   (a) Never-treated public firms in the same 2-digit SIC industry and NYSE size
       decile;  
   (b) “Not-yet-treated” firms provide additional within-industry counterfactual
       observations before their own adoption.

Treatment timing / event date  
   Day 0 = magazine news-stand release date (≈ one week before issue cover
   date).  The panel month containing Day 0 is coded as period t = 0.

Robustness: a propensity-score-matched control pool and an entropy-balanced
control will be used to verify that results are not driven by composition
differences.

======================================================================
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
----------------------------------------------------------------------
A1  Parallel trends.  Abnormal returns of soon-to-be-treated and control firms
    would have evolved similarly absent treatment.  
    Plausibility: Turnover on the list (≈⅓ per year) plus six-month lag between
    survey and publication makes anticipation difficult.  We can test by
    estimating leads (t = –36 … –1 months).

A2  No simultaneous confounders.  No other event systematically coincides with
    first-time listing and also drives returns.  
    Plausibility: Listing is unrelated to earnings announcement timing; we will
    drop firm-months in which M&A, seasoned equity offerings, or CEO turnover
    occur.

A3  Stable unit treatment value (SUTVA).  One firm’s inclusion does not change
    returns of another control firm.  
    Plausibility: Cross-firm spillovers are unlikely given diversified investor
    portfolios; we will nevertheless cluster s.e.’s by industry × year to allow
    correlated shocks.

A4  No selective survival.  Firms do not systematically delist as a consequence
    of treatment status.  
    Plausibility: Large, established firms; we will censor at delisting date and
    use inverse-probability weighting as a check.

======================================================================
4. Threats to Identification & Remedies
----------------------------------------------------------------------
T1  Unobserved time-varying firm quality (e.g., new strategy) could drive both
    satisfaction and returns.  
    • Include firm × linear time trend.  
    • Control for changes in advertising, R&D, and SG&A.  
    • Instrumental-variable robustness: use unexpected violations of Fortune’s
      list quota by industry (exogenous ranking pressure).

T2  Anticipation/leakage.  Employees answer surveys ~6-7 months earlier; news
    could leak.  
    • Placebo event windows at survey completion date.  
    • Exclude months –6 to –1 and verify no abnormal returns.

T3  Multiple treatment years.  Being listed repeatedly may have different
    effects.  
    • Estimate separate coefficients for first, second, … nth appearance.  
    • Apply Sun & Abraham (2021) estimator to deal with dynamic treatment
      effects and heterogeneous adoption timing.

======================================================================
5. R Code Outline
----------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
# ---------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)
library(fixest)       # fast high-dim FE regressions
library(did)          # Callaway & Sant'Anna ATT
library(EventStudy)   # for short-run CAR
library(lubridate)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Data Loading
# ---------------------------------------------------------
ret     <- fread("crsp_monthly.csv")      # PERMNO, date, ret, mkt_rf, smb, hml, rf
fortune <- fread("fortune_best.csv")      # CUSIP, pub_date (yyyy-mm-dd)
comp    <- fread("compustat_annual.csv")  # CUSIP, fiscal_year, size, bm, etc.

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Variable Construction
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Harmonise tickers/CUSIPs to PERMNO
fortune[, firm_id := match_cusip_to_permno(CUSIP)]        # pseudo-function

# Monthly panel
panel <- merge(ret, fortune[,.(firm_id, pub_date)],
               by = "firm_id", all.x = TRUE)

panel[, pub_month := floor_date(pub_date, "month")]
panel[, first_list_month := min(pub_month, na.rm = TRUE), by = firm_id]

# Treatment status & relative event time
panel[, treated := !is.na(first_list_month)]
panel[, rel_month := as.numeric(month(date) + 12*year(date) -
                                (month(first_list_month) + 12*year(first_list_month)))]
panel[, post := (rel_month >= 0) * treated]

# Excess return
panel[, excess_ret := ret - rf]

# Controls
panel <- merge(panel, comp, by = c("firm_id", "fiscal_year"), all.x = TRUE)

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Main DiD Regression
# ---------------------------------------------------------
spec <- feols(excess_ret ~ post*treated + size + bm |
              firm_id + date, data = panel,
              cluster = ~firm_id)

etable(spec)

# Dynamic leads/lags
dyn <- feols(excess_ret ~ i(rel_month, treated, ref = -1) + size + bm |
             firm_id + date, data = panel[rel_month >= -60 & rel_month <= 60],
             cluster = ~firm_id)

iplot(dyn, xlab = "Months relative to first listing")

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Robustness: staggered ATT (Callaway–Sant'Anna)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
cs <- att_gt(yname   = "excess_ret",
             gname   = "first_list_month",
             idname  = "firm_id",
             tname   = "date",
             xformla = ~ size + bm,
             data    = panel[year(date)>=1984 & year(date)<=2009])

summary(cs)
aggte(cs, type = "dynamic") %>% plot()

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Announcement Event Study (short-run)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
es <- event_study(ret_dt    = ret,
                  event_dt  = fortune[,.(firm_id, pub_date)],
                  id.var    = "firm_id",
                  event.var = "pub_date",
                  ret.var   = "ret",
                  mkt.var   = "mkt_rf",
                  window    = c(-5, 5))
print(es$car)
```

======================================================================
6. Expected Results
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Theory (human-capital view) predicts a positive effect.  Based on back-of-the-
envelope comparisons with quality-minus-junk or intangibles factor premia, I
expect:

•  Short-window CAR around announcement: +0.3 % to +0.7 % (small because many
   investors still under-react).

•  Long-run monthly alpha vs. Fama-French 3-factor model: +25 – 40 bp per month
   (≈ 3–5 % per year) beginning ~12 months after first listing.

======================================================================
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DiD)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
C1 Clear treatment timing …………………………… 1  
C2 Credible parallel trends (tested) …………… 1  
C3 No interference/spillovers ………………… 0.5  
C4 No differential attrition …………………… 0.5  
C5 Correct standard-error clustering ………… 1  

Total: 4 / 5.  The main residual concern is remaining unobserved shocks that
jointly raise satisfaction and performance, which we attempt to mitigate with
firm trends, rich controls, and dynamic lead checks.
